summary:
Held 0 of today's 10 biggest US movers.

• 6 upside misses — DD +186%, BLDR +11%, IQV +8%, CRL +8%, UAL +7%. These cleared the universe screen but no strategy picked them up; the morning brief either filtered them on a catalyst/RSI/earnings rule or had nothing positive to trigger an entry.

• 4 downside moves (APO -6%, BX -6%, HOOD -6%, ARES -6%) are unreachable on a long-only basket — no mechanism to express a short or pair-trade.

• Most instructive miss: DD (+185.99%) — DuPont executed a 1-for-3 reverse stock split effective June 24, 2026; the +186% close-to-close gain is a mechanical price artifact of the consolidation, not a fundamental or news-driven move. Why we passed: Outside any active strategy's universe. The +186% is a reverse-split artifact (1-for-3, eff. June 24), not a real gain — momentum/gap filters would flag this as a false positive without a corporate-action exclusion layer.

top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. The +186% is a reverse-split artifact (1-for-3, eff. June 24), not a real gain — momentum/gap filters would flag this as a false positive without a corporate-action exclusion layer.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a corporate-action filter that ingests daily 8-K/exchange announcements and blacklists tickers with an active reverse split from all gap/momentum scanners on the split effective date.

top_movers.catalyst: ROAD to Housing Act passed Congress June 22-23 (Senate 85-5, House 358-32), removing construction regulatory barriers; market continued to price in the housing supply tailwind on June 25, a direct demand catalyst for BLDR.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. BLDR (~$10B market cap, building materials) is a sector the bot doesn't cover. The catalyst was a multi-day legislative event (bill passage June 22-23), requiring a policy-trigger entry rather than intraday price/volume signals.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a housing-supply legislative trigger: when a major housing bill passes both chambers, flag direct-beneficiary names (BLDR, DOOR, CARR) for momentum entry next session open, gated on volume ≥1.2× 20-day average.

top_movers.catalyst: No new corporate event on Jun 25; continuation rally off Morgan Stanley upgrade to OW/$220 (Jun 17) + Lilly TuneLab nonclinical-testing collaboration (Jun 18); sector rotation into CRO/pharma-services as Nasdaq 100 sold off.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. CRL is a mid-large-cap CRO (pharma-services sector) not covered by the bot's tradable universe; the +8% move was a multi-day institutional accumulation following a week-old analyst upgrade, not an intraday gap-up signal that news-reactive or momentum strategies could act on.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a post-Tier-1-upgrade watchlist layer: when a name in the CRO/pharma-services peer group (CRL, IQV, MEDP) receives a ≥2-notch upgrade with ≥15% PT raise, stage it for momentum entry if price holds above the upgrade-day close for 3+ sessions — this captures delayed institutional rotation without chasing the initial

top_movers.catalyst: Crude oil fell below $70/barrel (multi-month low), cutting jet-fuel cost outlook, while UBS raised its UAL price target to $153 from $148 (Buy maintained), triggering a broad airline sector rally to 52-week highs.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. The move was a macro/sector tailwind (oil drop) combined with an analyst price-target lift — not a pre-market earnings gap or technical momentum signal — so no existing filter had a pathway to admit the name intraday.
top_movers.suggestion: Add an oil-price-shock universe gate: when crude drops ≥3% intraday, admit large-cap airline names (UAL, DAL, AAL) to the momentum strategy provided analyst consensus ≥ Buy, capturing sector-rotation tailwinds without requiring short capability.

top_movers.catalyst: WTI crude fell below $70 as the Strait of Hormuz began reopening following a Middle East peace deal, reversing BKNG's biggest 2026 travel headwind and triggering a broad sector rally.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. BKNG is a ~$181B mega-cap OTA (post-25-for-1 split, April 2026); the +7% gap was a geopolitical macro catalyst (oil price collapse / Strait of Hormuz reopening) that materialised pre-open before any intraday momentum or volume signal could fire.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a macro-travel trigger rule: when WTI crude drops ≥3% intraday, scan large-cap OTA names (BKNG, EXPE) for pre-open gaps ≥3% and allow a news-reactive long entry within the first 30 min of the session.

top_movers.catalyst: Apollo capped withdrawals from Apollo Debt Solutions retail private credit fund at 5% vs ~17% redemption requests (2nd consecutive quarter gate); SEC concurrently opened a valuation-practice and investor-disclosure probe.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — APO is a large-cap alt-asset manager in diversified financials. Move was catalyst-driven (redemption gate + SEC probe) with no pre-market technical signal for momentum or mean-reversion filters to act on.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a news-reactive short filter for large-cap financials: trigger on ≥5% gap-down + confirmed 'redemption gate' or 'SEC investigation' headline within 30 min of open to capture institutional liquidity-event selloffs.

top_movers.catalyst: Partners Group (Swiss PE peer) disclosed fund-level withdrawal restrictions, sparking sector-wide contagion across alt-asset managers; BX fell in sympathy amid its own BCRED redemption-limit overhang and CRE exposure concerns.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — BX is a large-cap alt-asset manager not covered by any momentum/mean-reversion filter. The drop was peer-contagion-driven (Partners Group news), not a BX-specific event; no single-name signal would have enabled pre-market positioning.
top_movers.suggestion: Add alt-asset managers (BX, KKR, APO) to the universe with a sector-contagion rule: when any peer announces fund redemption restrictions pre-market, auto-flag the group for a short-side fade at open with a ≥2% gap threshold.

top_movers.catalyst: Meta CEO Zuckerberg directed development of 'Arena', a prediction-markets app directly targeting Robinhood's fastest-growing event-contract business; a concurrent $2B convertible-note offering added dilution pressure.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. HOOD had already surged ~50% from April lows (~$70→$105), making it too extended for a fresh momentum entry; the reversal was headline-driven (direct competitor entry + capital-structure event), requiring pre-open news detection that purely technical strategies lack.
top_movers.suggestion: Seed a catalyst-reversal watchlist nightly from the top-50 prior-month momentum winners; gate intraday mean-reversion entries when a direct-competitor or capital-structure headline (convertible, secondary) crosses pre-market, targeting entry within the first 30 min of open.

top_movers.catalyst: Bloomberg reported Ares' Strategic Income Fund (~$11bn) capped redemptions at 5% after 14.4% of investors sought to exit (up from 11.6% prior quarter), reigniting private credit liquidity fears.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — ARES is a large-cap alternative asset manager. The drop was news-driven (fund redemption gate disclosure); no technical pre-signal exists for this event type, so momentum and mean-reversion filters had no edge.
top_movers.suggestion: Add large-cap alt-asset managers (ARES, APO, BX, KKR) to a news-reactive universe; trigger short entry on 8-K/PR keywords 'redemption cap' or 'gate' within 30 min of SEC filing, with a 3% stop-loss.
